reviewerOrPass: Worker A, same AI, separate source-first pass
method: Same AI, separate source-first pass after freezing. Started from the dated scheme and thesis entry, reconstructed all three years and checked the official ordering and published entry fields. Reconsidered operations research and mathematics alignments with the dated Groningen course descriptions and the active workbook before comparing the finished alternatives and audience record. Worker A performed both passes.
findings: Groningen’s English-taught BSc Econometrics and Operations Research, ISAT 56833, has 180 EC. The 2026–27 scheme supplies one common set of twelve 5 EC courses in each of the first two years and a common third-year scheme. The four advertised profiles describe areas of study. They do not establish four separate 180 EC comparator curricula. The third year consists of an approved 30 EC minor or foreign minor, a 5 EC EOR elective, three required 5 EC courses and a 10 EC individual thesis. The elective must come from the EOR list or be individually approved. The foreign minor is approved and subject to course level, overlap and relevance rules. No specific elective, minor or profile is chosen for the general comparator.

Year 1 starts with introductory calculus, OR modelling and data analytics, then programming, linear algebra and probability. Analysis follows those mathematics courses, with multivariate calculus, distributions and statistical modelling in block 2B. Year 2 places advanced linear algebra before convex optimisation, and probability and distributions before stochastic OR. OR Modelling precedes Discrete Operations Research. Linear Models precedes Introduction to Econometrics in 2A, which in turn precedes Dynamic Econometrics in 2B. Year 3 Numerical Methods expects programming and statistical inference. Games, Competition and Markets builds on second-year Game Theory. The normal thesis is in the second semester, with an alternative first-semester offering. Entry requires 120 EC, including all 60 EC of year one, and an approved 180 EC degree plan. Normal progression reaches this before the thesis. The thesis requires an individual scientific report with a mathematical model, methods and interpretation.

The closest schedule gives economics and econometrics substantive depth through economic models, regression, causal analysis and public economics, alongside calculus, probability, programming, numerical methods and optimisation. Ethics adds reasoning about decisions, and machine learning contributes predictive methods. Econometrics and Advanced Calculus are directly relevant on their course descriptions. The operations research option develops implementation through databases, software, algorithms, probability, decision modelling and optimisation, with reinforcement learning after the decision course. AI Ethics supports the evaluation of automated decisions. Its business context comes from venture foundations and organisational research. Neural networks supply additional modelling methods. The climate and policy direction adds climate science, environmental spatial analysis, life-cycle assessment and a renewable-energy project to economic and quantitative analysis. Sustainability Essentials II also provides preparation for system design. Linear Systems contributes signals, transformation and dynamic-system methods; it does not stand in for advanced linear algebra. OR Modelling pairs with actual constrained linear programming, Discrete OR with actual dynamic programming and network methods, and Stochastic Models with Markov models, each with different application coverage. Queueing, actuarial mathematics, specialist convexity and dynamic econometrics remain visible separately. Finance and probability can support risk reasoning, while the workbook offers no sustained combination of life contingencies, actuarial loss and reserve models or premiums. The actuarial decision rests on coverage, rather than offering gaps.
